question: Given exact full-method native recorded positive site×species masks, which currently source-unconfirmed site×species statuses would, if independently CERTIFIED truly absent, convert the four existing weakly one-sided (zero-allowed) category contrasts into a strict sign? Can candidate site visits be shared among two species?

source.study: Wenner et al. 2025, Global Ecology and Conservation 62 e03837, DOI 10.1016/j.gecco.2025.e03837; data Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.15044115 CC BY 4.0

fixed_assumptions: Every archived source-positive count is truly a positive binary site×species status (zero false positives), not validated independently.
A single static site×species status exists over the archived survey period, solely for illustrative logical bounds; ecological closure across 91 days is NOT shown.
Non-positive survey records mean UNKNOWN, never independently certified true absence; new negative witnesses are a COUNTERFACTUAL information scenario, NOT new field observations.
Each source-unconfirmed site×species may independently be truly present or truly absent; no other ecological constraints are assumed.
fixed_targets: derive ALL source-positive-only nonnegative_only and nonpositive_only category contrasts among 9 species × intervention-control, intervention-artificial, artificial-control; do not cherry-pick
for each weak one-sided contrast, list every original site in the incomplete category with no recorded positive of that species; no candidates from source-positive sites

simulate one independently certified true negative at each listed source-unconfirmed candidate; use [positive_count/n, (n-verified_absences)/n] for latent group-rate interval and compare exact integer difference signs
verify a SINGLE certified absence in incomplete group makes strict comparison sign for each weak one-sided case

enumerate exact minimum number of distinct source-site visits, assuming a revisit COULD independently certify more than one species negative at that same site, needed to cover all four comparisons; separate site count from number of independent species×site negative certificates
report all-site min-cover solutions and source-recorded prior visit dates and method-row presence for candidate sites, without assuming effort
for any candidate newly confirmed positive rather than negative, show the effect is to tighten the original bound but cannot independently certify strict sign with no true negative evidence
return source SHA gates, explicit code tests and result receipts, no models
hard_stops: Source non-detection is not a certified true negative, including repeated non-detection or absence of dipnet CSV rows.

Do not claim 2 field visits WILL identify a strict biological effect; 2 is a conditional best-case combinatorial site cover if true absence certificates can be obtained for two species at each target site, something the data DO NOT currently support.
An actual field survey may only support detection-probability modeling, not logically perfect absence; site choice requires location/permissions/field protocol and biological temporal definition.
Study sites and wetland categories were observational, not randomized: strict site-level status difference is not a causal restoration effect.
No new occupancy, movement, A/B/M causal attribution, statistical power, p-values, actual ecological world enumeration or fourth EOG-WF scored endpoint; keep PR #697 Draft/unmerged.
